findings.claim: lineageOf now starts from a nil slice and returns nil when the observation has only one part; combined with the removal of the observation identity, a memory imported as a single part has an empty lineage. Callers that previously relied on at least one lineage identity (the observation) to bridge a legacy page keyed by it now get nothing. The commit states this is intended (S7), but no test in the diff asserts the single-part case besides memory 2 (nil). Consider documenting that a single-part import has no lineage at all.

mirrorsOf comment says it returns memories 'each as every memory of its parts', but the loop does not filter out card.ID itself; unchanged behavior, yet with the observation identity removed an imported part set holding the card's own id would now yield a self-mirror with no other marker. Low risk, not shown reachable since mirrorsOf applies only to cards with no import_map row.

evidence: Diff removes engramSource constant and observation identities from lineageOf and mirrorsOf; tests updated consistently.
MemoryByEngramID and its tests removed in store.go and store_test.go; the diff cannot show remaining callers, but the commit states it is unused (compile-time check not visible in diff).
MemoryIDsByEngramIDs is retained and still supplies k.parts.
